FORGE Map: incidents from South African news, checked by hand

A free map of hand-checked incidents from South African news, each linked to its sources. You can view the map and download the data as CSV or JSON without signing in. Pin counts show what FORGE Map has checked, not how much crime happens anywhere.

How old a pin is

The dot's colour is its category. The ring around it shows how long ago the incident happened, counted from the incident date in South African time. The live map shows the last 30 days.

  • Thick, solid ring: happened 0 to 2 days ago
  • Medium ring: 3 to 7 days ago
  • Thin, fainter ring: 8 to 14 days ago
  • Thin, dashed ring: 15 to 29 days ago
  • No ring: older than the 30-day live map. It shows only when you open it or a date lookup finds it, and says which month's archive it's from.
  • White diamond: updated in the last 7 days with a new development. An update never changes the ring, because age counts from the incident.
  • Soft halo that slowly pulses: added to the map in the last 48 hours. Pins added together don't pulse in step. With Motion off, or if your device asks for reduced motion, the halo stays still. An update doesn't restart it.
  • 3
    White dot on a numbered circle: the group holds a pin added in the last 48 hours. Numbered circles never pulse.

The Motion switch with the map buttons turns the pulse off, and the map remembers that on this device.

Earlier months, with the map buttons, opens one whole month from the archive. There the pins are hollow, with no ring and no pulse, the map turns grey inside a dashed frame, and a banner names the month and says it's not the live map. Back to live map returns here.

The date it happened, or the date a body was found. Never the report date: where a report gives only that, the record is counted as date not stated. An arrest, charge or court step in an older case is counted apart, not on the day of that step. Days with no records show as zero.
